# Chesterton's Fence

<p class="lens-meta"><code class="lens-code">CHESTERTON</code> · Modern — analytic and scientific method · <strong>Catalogued — a reading, owns no gate</strong></p>

## The failure it names

removing something without recovering why it was put there

## What it does

a `supersedes` edge requires a recorded reason the prior existed

## Worked example

Before the fence comes down, the reason it went up must be stated — not because the reason is necessarily good, but because not knowing it is not an argument.

## Sources

- G. K. Chesterton, The Thing (1929), ch. 4 "The Drift from Domesticity"
